title: A punto de + infinitivo: al borde de que algo ocurra

sections.content: Estar a punto de + infinitive (to be about to, on the verge of) marks the closest possible brush with something that almost happened but didn't -- exactly the language a reading about thirteen days in October 1962 needs. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El mundo entero estuvo a punto de vivir una guerra nuclear directa entre Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética.
items.english: The entire world came close to experiencing a direct nuclear war between the United States and the Soviet Union.

items.spanish: Ambas superpotencias estuvieron a punto de entrar en un conflicto armado directo.
items.english: Both superpowers came close to entering a direct armed conflict.

items.spanish: Muchos historiadores consideran este el momento más peligroso de toda la Guerra Fría.
items.english: Many historians consider this the most dangerous moment of the entire Cold War.

items.spanish: La crisis se resolvió finalmente mediante una negociación secreta.
items.english: The crisis was ultimately resolved through a secret negotiation.

sections.content: Estuvo a punto de + infinitive always implies the event did NOT actually happen -- estuvo a punto de vivir una guerra nuclear means the war was narrowly avoided, not that it broke out. Don't confuse it with acabar por, which marks something that did eventually happen.
